instructions: Rinse the rice and cook it in 1 3/4 cups water, covered, the way you usually do.
Cut the wings at the joints into drumettes and flats if they're whole. Pat them dry. Slice 3 thin slices of ginger.
Heat a large deep skillet or wok over high heat until a drop of water sizzles in it. Add the 2 tbsp oil and the ginger. Stand back a little, since the oil will spatter.
Add the wings in a single layer. Cook for 3 minutes on each side, until they're lightly browned.
Pour in the cola, 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine, 1 tbsp dark soy sauce and 2 tbsp light soy sauce. Bring it to a boil, cover, and turn the heat down to medium.
Simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, until most of the sauce is gone and just a small pool is left.
Stir the wings and add the 1/4 tsp salt. Take out the ginger.

Turn the heat back up to high and stir quickly for 1 to 2 minutes, until the sauce coats each wing. You're cooking them to 175°F, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest wing. No thermometer? Cut into one: the juices should run clear.
Serve the wings with the steamed rice.
method_notes: The Woks of Life (4.58 from 26 ratings) leads: brown the wings in a hot wok, add regular cola, Shaoxing wine and both soy sauces, simmer covered, then boil down the last of the sauce to a glaze. Omnivore's Cookbook (5.0 from 12 ratings) sears first, adds scallion and dried chili and boils uncovered for 20 minutes, and agrees that diet cola won't work. This version leaves out the optional orange peel, cinnamon and chili to stay mild. The wings are written as a dinner for four with rice.
